To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zinc absorption is delayed by phytate, and that the presence of phytic acid in a test meal can be used to assess zinc absorption from various test meals.
the disappearance of Zn from the intestine was delayed in rats fed soy protein isolate ( SPI) probably because of the phytate content of the soy.
the disappearance of intestinal zinc is delayed in rats consuming soy protein, probably due to the presence of phytic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relationship between the level of zinc in the small intestinal content and the level of CP activity in the intestinal contents of rats fed a test meal containing casein, soy protein isolate or egg white.
the effect of dietary protein sources and their amino acid composition on zinc absorption in the small intestine.
the effect of dietary protein source on the postprandially induced increase in zinc concentration and CP activity in the intestinal contents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zinc is not a growth limiting factor for rats fed SPI.
dietary protein source affects the disappearance of zinc and the activity of CPA and CPD in the small intestinal tract.
dietary protein sources can affect intestinal zinc and carboxipeptidase A activity in rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of phytic acid in SPI delayed the absorption of zinc, but the presence of trypsin inhibitors in EW did not delay the absorption of zinc from the small intestine.
zinc and CP activities in the small intestine are influenced by the type of protein consumed.
zinc and CP activity in the intestinal contents of rats are dependent on the dietary protein source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zinc is more available from casein than from soy protein or egg white.
the amount of zinc available to intestinal cells is dependent on the type of protein consumed.
dietary proteins may affect zinc absorption and retention in rats.
